# REGIME READ — 2026-09-15

**[FULL READ — WebSearch available, second consecutive full run.]** Everything material has been refreshed. **One large new macro fact (the 10-year Treasury yield traded through 5% for the first time since 2023) and one large new equity-specific fact (a coordinated AI-industry call to slow development, which took the semiconductor index down 5.9% in a session).** The option chain fetched successfully this run, so Layer 2 uses a real quote rather than the heuristic. **One data conflict is unresolved and is flagged rather than smoothed over: the Brent row.**

## Changes Since Previous Read
- **Stage: 3 (Neutral/choppy) → 3 (Neutral/choppy)** — unchanged for a fourteenth consecutive read. **VIX 17.10 sits inside the 15–22 band, and the classification is still held by that single number.** Breadth remains at correction-grade levels.
- **Total score: −9 → −9 (delta 0).** **No lens moved.** The composition is unchanged: 0 bullish, 5 bearish, 2 neutral — **sixth consecutive read with no bullish lens.**
- **Triggers from previous read:**
  - *Bearish — TQQQ closes below the 4-week low $67.93:* **DID NOT FIRE.** **TQQQ closed $69.27 on 2026-09-14 (−2.41%)**, which is **1.97% above** the old line. **Note the line itself moved: the rolling 20-session window dropped $67.93 and the 4-week low is now $67.34, so spot is 2.79% above the current low.** The premarket estimate in the last read (≈$67.89 from a −1.45% QQQ premarket) **overstated the damage** — TQQQ fell 2.41%, not 4.35%.
  - *Bearish — VIX above 20:* **ARMED, and further away than it looked.** **VIX 17.10, unchanged on the day** (2026-09-15). Needs **+16.96%**. **The "17.50" I printed last read was a pre-open quote; the VIX settled 2026-09-14 at 17.10.** This is exactly the basis distinction the withdrawn Finding 3 was about, and the snapshot handled it correctly.
  - *Bearish — VXN > 25:* **ARMED and moved closer.** **VXN 22.05, +4.90%** — it gave back roughly half of the previous session's 9.90% crush. Needs **+13.38%** (was +18.93%).
  - *Bearish — NDX < 28,400:* **ARMED and closer.** NDX **29,127.16 (−0.82%)** needs **−2.50%** (was −3.30%).
  - *Bearish — HY OAS through 3.25% WITH IG above 0.90%:* **ARMED and moved AWAY — credit tightened.** **HY OAS 2.65% (−5bp), IG OAS 0.80% (unchanged)**, both stamped **2026-09-11** (FRED). Needs **+60bp** on HY. **These readings are now three days stale and predate the 10-year breaking 5%, the AI selloff and the pipeline attack.** Credit remains the single most important unobserved variable in this report.
  - *Bearish — Brent above $105 on two consecutive closes:* **ONE LEG CONFIRMED, SECOND LEG UNRESOLVED — I am not scoring it either way.** Backing out the snapshot's own arithmetic, **Brent settled 2026-09-14 at $105.68** (above the line). For 09-15 the engine reports **$101.15 (−4.29%)** while web sources report Brent trading **$106.96** ([Yahoo Finance live, Sep 15](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-september-15-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-081307838.html)) **to $107.82** ([ING, Sep 15](https://think.ing.com/articles/the-commodities-feed-oil-stronger-on-saudi-pipeline-shutdown140926)). **Those cannot both be right, today's session has not settled, and I will not resolve a trigger on a number I cannot reconcile.** See the footnote.
  - *Bullish — TQQQ reclaims the 50DMA and holds two sessions:* **ARMED and moved away.** Spot **$69.27** against a 50DMA of **$70.97** — **−2.40%**, having been 0.10% away. The dime-wide near-miss resolved downward, as the premarket suggested.
  - *Bullish — NDX ≥ 30,000 with VXN < 19:* **ARMED, both legs widened.** NDX needs **+3.00%** (was +2.15%); VXN needs **−13.83%** (was −9.61%).
  - *Bullish — Brent back below $92:* **ARMED.** Distance depends entirely on which Brent print is correct: **−9.05%** on the engine's $101.15, **−13.98%** on the web-verified $106.96.
  - *Bullish — FOMC dovish surprise:* **PENDING — the decision is tomorrow.** **Odds moved the other way: CME FedWatch now shows roughly 93% probability of a 25bp hike** ([Yahoo Finance, 2026-09-15](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-september-15-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-081307838.html)), up from **84.1% on 09-14** and 85% at the last read.
  - *Bullish — early US–China tariff-reduction announcement:* **ARMED, nothing new.** The Washington summit remains scheduled for **2026-09-24**.
  - *Neutralizer — FOMC 2026-09-16:* **the two-day meeting began today.** It is now session 2 of the window rather than session 3.
- **Notable lens flips: none.** **Two lenses were considered for a downgrade and both were held, deliberately — see Lens 3 and Lens 6.**

**Monday 2026-09-14 was a red session with a very unusual internal shape, and the headline index moves badly understate it.** **SPX −0.48% to 7,619.98, Nasdaq Composite −0.56%, NDX −0.82%, DJI −0.29% (−152 points), Russell 2000 −0.40%** — all modest. **Underneath, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 5.9%, Nvidia −3.4% and Intel −5.6%** ([Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-14/asian-stocks-to-fall-on-ai-key-us-yield-tops-5-markets-wrap), [CNN Business](https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/14/business/ai-stocks-slide-slowdown-development-amodei-altman-intl)). **At the intraday lows SPX was −0.8% and the Nasdaq −1.3% before recovering.** In plain terms: a 5.9% fall in the chip complex produced a 0.8% fall in the Nasdaq-100, which means the rest of the index absorbed it — **that is a rotation, not a broad liquidation, and it is the one genuinely constructive thing in this report.**

**Two causes, both new since the last read.** **First: the 10-year Treasury yield rose to as high as 5.01% on Monday, the first time above 5% since October 2023, and reached 5.041% on Tuesday** ([Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-14/us-10-year-yield-breaches-5-as-inflation-supply-worries-mount), [CNN](https://www.cnn.com/2026/09/14/investing/bond-yields-market-turmoil), [Yahoo live](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-september-15-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-081307838.html)). **The yfinance row above shows 4.961 as a settled close on 09-14 — the 5.01% was an intraday print, and both are true.** **Second: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a ~3,800-word essay on Saturday 2026-09-12 calling for the industry to deliberately slow the rate at which model capabilities improve, and Sam Altman and Elon Musk both said they agree** ([Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/12/anthropic-ai-amodei-pacing), [ABC News](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-09-13/anthropic-ceo-calls-for-slower-ai-development/107147650), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/12/anthropics-amodei-proposes-plan-to-slow-the-pace-of-advancing-ai-capabilities.html)). **The three people running the most advanced AI labs publicly agreeing to go slower is a direct challenge to the earnings path priced into the AI capital-expenditure complex, and the chip tape reacted accordingly.**

**Today, Tuesday 2026-09-15, futures are lower into the Fed: Dow futures −0.2% to −0.40%, S&P 500 futures −0.2% to −0.30%, Nasdaq-100 futures −0.1% to −0.32%** ([Yahoo live](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-september-15-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-081307838.html), [Benzinga](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/prediction-markets/26/09/61781323/stock-market-will-sp-500-open-up-or-down-today-37)). **VIX is 17.10, unchanged.** **These are premarket quotes, not closes, and no trigger in this report is evaluated on them.**

Both reasonable.** **Brent implies a 09-14 settle of $105.68 against a quoted $108.48 — also reasonable — but its 09-15 level of $101.15 cannot be reconciled with any web source today. That one row is flagged, not trusted, and not used to resolve a trigger.**

## Regime Stage Tracker
- **Current Stage:** **3 — Neutral / choppy**, held by the VIX level and nothing else, for a second consecutive read. **VIX 17.10 is inside the 15–22 band; VXN 22.05 likewise.** **No Stage-4 threshold has fired: VIX needs +16.96% to reach 20, VXN needs +13.38% to reach 25, NDX needs −2.50%, HY OAS needs +60bp.** **The "breadth deteriorating" half of the Stage-4 definition remains satisfied — roughly 37.77% of S&P 500 members are above their 50-day average as of 2026-09-14** ([MacroMicro](https://en.macromicro.me/series/18331/sp500-50ma-breadth)) **— but the VIX condition is explicit and it is not met.** **Scoring conservatively, between Stage 3 and Stage 4 I take the one the stated thresholds support: Stage 3.** **What a reader should carry away is that this is the second read in a row where one number, and only one number, separates the two.**
- **Stage Anchor:** **2026-08-28 — Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote**, which moved implied September hike odds from roughly 30% to a majority ([CNBC 2026-08-28](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/-september-fed-decision-now-a-coin-flip-as-rate-hike-odds-increase.html), [CNBC 2026-08-31](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/31/markets-see-warsh-endorsing-a-rate-hike-in-september-not-everyone-is-convinced.html)). **The anchor resolves tomorrow at 93% implied.** The **US–Iran conflict** (from 2026-02-28) amplifies through the oil-and-yields channel.
- **Position:** **Week 3 of the rate-repricing leg, on its final full day** — the decision the leg has been building toward is tomorrow. Stage-3 range confirmed across fourteen consecutive reads (08-28 through 09-15).
- **Confidence:** **High.** Five lenses bearish (Macro −2, Breadth −2, Cross-asset −2, Geopolitical −2, Dealer flow −1), none bullish, two neutral. **No degradation cap: WebSearch was available, the option chain fetched, and macro, breadth, sentiment and geopolitical inputs were all verified today.**
- **Bullish trigger (→ Stage 2):** NDX ≥ **30,000** (+3.00%) **with** VXN below **19** (−13.83%); **or** a dovish FOMC surprise tomorrow — no hike against 93% odds, or a hike with a dot plot showing no further moves; **or** Brent sustainably below **$92**; **or** a credible walk-back of the AI-slowdown agreement that restores the semiconductor complex.
- **Bearish trigger (→ Stage 4):** VIX sustained above **20** (+16.96% — **still the sole hinge of the stage classification**); **or** **VXN > 25** (+13.38%); **or** NDX < **28,400** (−2.50%); **or** **HY OAS through 3.25% with IG above 0.90%** (from 2.65% / 0.80%, both stamped 09-11).

## Regime Verdict
A Stage-3 range still held together by the VIX level alone — the 10-year yield has broken 5% for the first time since 2023, a near-certain rate hike and a fresh dot plot land tomorrow, the AI capital-expenditure story took its first coordinated insider challenge and dropped the chip index 5.9% in a session, breadth remains at correction-grade levels, and no lens in this report is positive — at **High** confidence.

**Data note.** WebSearch was available and the option chain fetched successfully, so this is a full read. **What I could NOT resolve: the Brent level for 2026-09-15, where the engine and three web sources disagree by roughly $6.** **What is stale: HY OAS 2.65% and IG OAS 0.80% both carry 2026-09-11 FRED stamps, so credit has not been observed across the 10-year breaking 5%, the AI selloff or the pipeline attack.** **Never retrieved in any read:** AAII, CFTC COT, margin debt, ETF flows, Citi Economic Surprise, insider/buyback activity, Copper/Gold, transports. **NAAIM remains paywalled since 2026-08-01.**

## Diverging Signals

**First, and it is the most interesting thing in this read: the semiconductor index fell 5.9% and the S&P 500 fell 0.48%.** **Nvidia −3.4%, Intel −5.6%, SOX −5.9%, against NDX −0.82% and SPX −0.48%** ([Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-14/asian-stocks-to-fall-on-ai-key-us-yield-tops-5-markets-wrap)). **For that arithmetic to work, money that left chips went somewhere else inside the index rather than leaving equities.** **That is the healthiest single fact in this report and I want to name it clearly, because almost everything else here is negative.** **But it sits directly on top of the opposite fact: only 37.77% of S&P members are above their 50-day average. So the index is simultaneously showing internal resilience on one day and internal damage over a month. The honest reading is that Monday was a rotation inside a market that is already thin — a good day's behaviour in a bad structural position, not evidence the structure has improved.**

**Second: the AI-slowdown story is a new KIND of risk for this instrument, and it does not look like the others in this report.** **Amodei's essay argued the industry should deliberately slow how fast model capabilities improve, and Altman and Musk agreed** ([Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/09/12/anthropic-ai-amodei-pacing), [ABC](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2026-09-13/anthropic-ceo-calls-for-slower-ai-development/107147650)). **Every other risk in this report is a price or a policy: a yield, a hike probability, a barrel of oil. This one is the people who build the product saying the product should be built more slowly, which speaks directly to the capital-expenditure path that the NDX's largest weights are valued on.** **It is unscheduled, it has no calendar entry, it cannot be hedged against an event date, and it is specific to the Nasdaq-100 rather than the broad market — which is exactly why SOX fell 5.9% while DJI fell 0.29%.** **For a leveraged Nasdaq instrument this is a more direct exposure than anything the macro lenses are measuring.**

**Third: credit tightened, and it is the only risk-supportive macro number in the report — and it is three days old.** **HY OAS came IN 5bp to 2.65% and IG held 0.80%, both stamped 2026-09-11.** **That is a genuinely calm credit market. It is also a credit market that had not yet seen the 10-year break 5%, the semiconductor complex fall 5.9%, or the pipeline attack resolve.** **For fourteen reads credit has been described as the member holding this report at Stage 3. It may still be doing that job. The reader should know that the single most reassuring number here is also among the oldest.**
